research_question: Which cycle-level sensor features most reliably separate stable healthy hydraulic component states from degraded cooler, valve, pump, and accumulator states, and can those verified signals support an interpretable troubleshooting sequence without a black-box model?

analysis_scope.public_dataset: UCI Condition monitoring of hydraulic systems
analysis_scope.discovery_verification_split: alternating repeated cycles within each stable 4-component factorial cell
analysis_scope.model_type: matched factorial signal screening; no machine-learning classifier

verification_criteria.note: Engineering repeatability screen; not a claim of statistical significance or field diagnostic performance.

spc_status.reason: Only 10 cycles are simultaneously stable and fully healthy across all four components. They are kept as a descriptive reference window; no in-control production baseline is claimed.

claim_boundaries: Observed findings describe this public experimental test rig only.
The source experiment deliberately varied component condition labels; matched holdout repeatability strengthens signal attribution but does not prove field causation on other equipment.
No maintenance intervention, downtime reduction, savings, safety improvement, or sustainment outcome was observed.
Source-flagged non-static cycles are excluded from component-effect estimation.
The second pass added matched comparisons and time-localized windows because whole-cycle summaries can average away dynamic switching behavior; thresholds were not loosened after the first pass.
